title: Mussels Mariniere
subtitle: Steamed mussels in white wine, shallots, and parsley
excerpt: Fresh mussels steamed open in a fragrant broth of dry white wine, shallots, garlic, and butter, finished with parsley and cream. Spectacular to look at and ready in under 15 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moules marinieres (mussels in the sailor's style) is one of the most iconic dishes of the Franco-Belgian and Norman culinary traditions, and is considered Belgium's national dish. The dish is associated with the coastal regions of northern France and Belgium, where mussels have been farmed for centuries in the tidal waters of the English Channel. The preparation is the simplest possible: mussels steamed in white wine with aromatics. The cooking broth becomes the sauce, flavoured by the juice released by the mussels as they open. The dish is quick, dramatic, and generously yielding: a 1 kg bag of mussels, which costs very little, produces a heaped bowl sufficient for two people as a main course. It is traditionally served with thick-cut chips and bread to mop up the broth. The key to good moules marinieres is freshness: mussels should be cooked on the day of purchase and any that do not close when tapped before cooking, or do not open after cooking, should be discarded.

recipeTools.notes: A very large lidded saucepan or casserole, large enough to hold all the mussels with room to steam open.

content.text: Scrub and debeard the mussels before cooking: pull out any stringy threads (the beard) by pulling towards the hinge end of the mussel. Discard any mussels that are cracked, or that stay open when tapped firmly on the side of the sink. Once the mussels are in the pan and the lid is on, they steam open in 3 to 4 minutes: check at 3 minutes and remove any that have opened. Return the lid and cook for 1 more minute for any remaining. Discard any that remain closed after 5 minutes total.

items.preparation: scrubbed and debearded; discard any that stay open when tapped

content.text: Melt the butter in a very large lidded saucepan over medium heat. Add the shallots and garlic and cook for 3 minutes until soft. Add the wine, thyme, and bay. Bring to a boil.
Tip in all the mussels. Cover immediately and cook over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until the mussels have opened. Discard any that remain closed.

Lift the mussels into deep warm bowls with a slotted spoon. Add the cream to the cooking broth and bubble for 1 minute. Season with pepper (no salt is needed as the mussels are naturally salty). Pour the broth over the mussels. Scatter with parsley. Serve with crusty bread.
